title: Microsoft 365 Backup: Full Workload Backup policies for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange
summary: Hold: all three admin-center paths omit the Settings navigation step. The protection command creates an inactive policy rather than enabling protection, despite its placement beside the enable control. The rollout dates, consumption pricing and documented workload behavior are supported.

claims.claim: The full admin-center route to the SharePoint control is Microsoft 365 Backup > Back up sites > All sites.
claims.quote: 1. Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center. 2. Select Settings. 3. Select Microsoft 365 Backup from the list of products.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Back up sites > All sites'. The cited page documents Settings before Microsoft 365 Backup and documents Back up sites > All sites under Enable Full Workload Backup.

claims.claim: The printed New-MgBetaSolutionBackupRestoreSharePointProtectionPolicy call performs the row's control of enabling workload protection.
claims.quote: Create a protection policy for a M365 service SharePoint. Policy will be created in inactive state.
claims.fix: Narrow controls[0].governs and the matching rendered row heading to 'Creation of a Full Workload Backup policy'. Keep the existing note that the command creates an inactive policy, not an activated one. This makes the control match the documented operation without presenting policy creation as enabling protection.

claims.claim: The creation cmdlet creates an inactive SharePoint policy.
claims.quote: Create a protection policy for a M365 service SharePoint. Policy will be created in inactive state.

claims.claim: Microsoft.Graph.Beta.BackupRestore documents the named creation cmdlet with DisplayName and ProtectionMode parameters.
claims.quote: Microsoft.Graph.Beta.BackupRestore Module ... New-MgBetaSolutionBackupRestoreSharePointProtectionPolicy ... [-DisplayName <string>] ... [-ProtectionMode <string>]

claims.claim: fullServiceBackup is the SharePoint protectionMode value for backing up an entire workload.
claims.quote: When set to fullServiceBackup, the entire workload is backed up and specific sites can be excluded using exclusion units.

claims.claim: Learn describes the setup experience as the same for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange, using SharePoint as its example.
claims.quote: The setup experience is the same for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange. The following example uses SharePoint.

claims.claim: The full exclusion route starts Microsoft 365 Backup > Backup policies > Full Workload Backup policy > View details > Excluded > Exclude more > Upload a CSV file containing the protection units to exclude.
claims.quote: Select Settings. ... Select Microsoft 365 Backup from the list of products. ... Open the Excluded tab. ... Select Exclude more. ... Upload a CSV file containing the protection units that you want to exclude.
claims.fix: Replace the front-matter and rendered-table path with 'Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Backup policies > Full Workload Backup policy > View details > Excluded > Exclude more > Upload a CSV file containing the protection units to exclude'. The CSV instruction is supported despite the pre-check's wording mismatch; the missing Settings selection is the fault.

claims.claim: The printed beta POST siteExclusionUnitsBulkAdditionJobs endpoint adds SharePoint sites as exclusion units.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/solutions/backupRestore/sharePointProtectionPolicies/845457dc-4bb2-4815-bef3-8628ebd1952e/siteExclusionUnitsBulkAdditionJobs

claims.claim: Up to 10,000 protection units can be excluded in a single operation.
claims.quote: You can exclude up to 10,000 protection units in a single operation.

claims.claim: The exclusion request body uses displayName and siteWebUrls.
claims.quote: | displayName | String | The display name of the bulk addition job. Required. | ... | siteWebUrls | String collection | The URLs of SharePoint sites to be added as exclusion units. Required. |

claims.claim: The exclusion operation requires BackupRestore-Configuration.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: | Delegated (work or school account) | BackupRestore-Configuration.ReadWrite.All | Not available. | ... | Application | BackupRestore-Configuration.ReadWrite.All | Not available. |

claims.claim: The full admin-center notification route is Microsoft 365 Backup > Email notifications.
claims.quote: Select Settings. ... Select Microsoft 365 Backup from the list of products. ... Go to the Email notifications option on the Microsoft 365 Backup home page.
claims.fix: Replace the front-matter and rendered-table path with 'Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Email notifications', as documented by the setup page.

claims.claim: The printed Update-MgSolutionBackupRestoreEmailNotificationSetting call enables notifications, opts into policy updates and sets a custom recipient.
claims.quote: [-AdditionalEvents <string>] ... [-IsEnabled] ... [-Recipients <IMicrosoftGraphNotificationRecipients>] ... [CustomRecipients <IMicrosoftGraphEmailIdentity[]>] ... [Email <String>] ... [Role <String>]
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/emailnotificationssetting?view=graph-rest-1.0 to sources. It documents additionalEvents=restoreAndPolicyUpdates, the literal used by the command; the cited cmdlet page names notificationEventsType but does not enumerate its values.

claims.claim: Global admins and Microsoft 365 Backup admins can enable general Backup notifications and update the notification list.
claims.quote: Global admins and Microsoft 365 Backup admins can turn on this feature and update the notification list at any time.

claims.claim: The Exchange policy-creation steps do not list a back-up-all option.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Exchange "Back up all mailboxes" "Choose selection method". Read the Exchange creation steps in backup-view-edit-policies: CSV, dynamic rule and filters are listed, with no back-up-all choice.

claims.claim: From Backup policies, selecting the Full Workload Backup policy and Turn off Full Workload Backup turns that policy off.
claims.quote: On the Backup policies page, select the Full Workload Backup policy for the workload. ... Select Turn off Full Workload Backup either from the command bar or the policy details pane.

claims.claim: Routine notification events are enabled using the optional checkbox in notification setup.
claims.quote: (Optional) Select the checkbox to also receive routine event notifications.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice describes the CSV upload on the Exclude sites step as optional.
claims.quote: (Optional) Upload a CSV file on the Exclude sites step to exclude specific sites from the scope of the policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice instructs administrators to review the coverage summary before confirming policy creation.
claims.quote: Review the coverage summary and confirm to create the Full Workload Backup policy.

claims.claim: These Microsoft 365 Backup controls operate at tenant scope.
claims.quote: Only tenant-level admins can create and manage backups using Microsoft 365 Backup for their users. ... When enabled, Microsoft 365 Backup sends email alerts to a Backup Notification List whenever an important backup event occurs.
